transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check.

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing some light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be able to get back to that fairly soon.

Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the info! Yes, I have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

Just make sure you store it as directed on the bottle - some products need to be kept in the fridge and others at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you! I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. 

Are you having severe pain or redness along with the light sensitivity?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, I'll keep that in mind. Yes, I do have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. This should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, it's been a few days since the surgery. That answers all my questions for now. I appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
